title: Construction of pullback on scheme descent data
statement: Let S,X,X′ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], a:X→S and r:X′→X any morphisms. There is a functor F:DD(a)→DD(r≫a) [def-galois-scheme-descent-data-category] and projections q_A from the underlying scheme of F(A) to that of A. Every square with q_A, the two structure maps and r is a pullback [def-pc-fibre-product], its datum satisfies IsBaseChange [def-pd-descent-datum], and F maps morphisms to their pullbacks: F(f).hom.left≫q_B=q_A≫f.hom.left.

proof.text: For each datum A, take the concrete chosen pullback V_A = A.V ×_X X′. Apply exists_canonical_pullback_descent_datum with g = r≫a to equip V_A with its datum E_A and its base-change equation. The witness is selected from an already proved theorem; the pullback projection equations also uniquely determine its transport.

For f:A→B define its pullback map by lifting (fst≫f.hom.left,snd). To check transport compatibility, compare both projections. For fst, apply the base-change equations for A and B, the original compatibility f.commutes, and associativity; for snd, both maps are over the same new base point. Pullback hom_ext and OverMorphism.ext give the equality.

Identity and composition of the lifted maps follow by comparing the two pullback projections. These maps define F. Set q_A = fst; pullback.condition supplies its commutativity equation, IsPullback.of_hasPullback gives the cartesian square, the chosen datum supplies IsBaseChange, and pullback.lift_fst gives q naturality.

proof_origin.note: J3: reuse the proved canonical objectwise datum, then directly construct morphism maps and prove compatibility and functor laws by the two pullback projections. No new holes or statements.
